sentences.text: Microvenator is a genus of small theropod dinosaur belonging to the Oviraptorosauria group.
The holotype fossil — the specimen the species is based on — is an incomplete skeleton likely belonging to a juvenile measuring 1.3 meters in length.
Barnum Brown erroneously included Deinonychus teeth with the Microvenator type specimen, leading him to informally name the specimen 'Megadontosaurus' meaning 'big-toothed lizard'.
Microvenator is considered a primitive taxon and may be the sister group to all other oviraptorosaurs.
Barnum Brown collected the type specimen AMNH 3041 in 1933.
John Ostrom later referred a single tooth from the Yale Peabody Museum collection (YPM 5366) to Microvenator.
Microvenator likely had a carnivorous diet, though an omnivorous tendency is not ruled out.
Microvenator coexisted with dinosaurs such as Deinonychus, Sauropelta, and Acrocanthosaurus.
Microvenator is the earliest known member of the oviraptorosaurian group from North America.
Microvenator is classified within the infraorder Oviraptorosauria and belongs to the family Oviraptoridae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Microvenator as Caenagnathidae.
Microvenator lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 110 million years ago, in the Aptian stage.
Microvenator fossils have been discovered in the states of Montana and Wyoming, USA.
It is unclear why some sources attribute Microvenator to the genus Microraptor.
